subject: Culture
title: Cultural Erasure on the Menu
description: A short lesson to help you apply Cultural Erasure on the Menu.

hook.text: Australian Aboriginal food traditions survived 60,000 years but nearly vanished in 200 years of colonization.

buildup.text: Colonial governments replaced Indigenous diets with European rations. Traditional knowledge was suppressed.

discovery.text: Native American boarding schools banned traditional foods. Children were forced to eat foreign meals.

twist.text: Today, Indigenous food movements are reclaiming ancestral ingredients. Bush tucker is back in fine dining.

climax.text: Destroying a people's food system attacks their identity at the root. It starves culture, not just bodies.

punchline.text: Erase the recipe and you erase the people.

details.summary: Cultural erasure on the menu occurs when colonialism, globalization, or assimilation pressure destroys indigenous food traditions. From Native American forced diet changes in boarding schools to the replacement of traditional crops with colonial cash crops, food erasure is cultural destruction.
details.whyItMatters: Recognizing food erasure reveals how dominant cultures destroy identity through diet. Reclaiming traditional foods is increasingly seen as an act of cultural resistance and healing.
takeaways: Native American boarding schools deliberately replaced indigenous diets
Colonial agriculture replaced traditional crops with cash crops worldwide
Indigenous food revitalization movements reclaim traditional diets

faq.question: How did colonialism erase food cultures?
faq.answer: Colonial powers replaced diverse local crops with export-oriented monocultures — sugar, coffee, rubber, cotton. Traditional farming knowledge was devalued.

faq.question: What is the indigenous food sovereignty movement?
faq.answer: Indigenous communities worldwide are reclaiming traditional foods as cultural resistance. Organizations like the Sioux Chef in Minnesota revive pre-colonial ingredients. Aboriginal Australian bush food is being rehabilitated.
